newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: More gains in some Singapore tech stocks-analysts.
newsitem.headline: More gains in some Singapore tech stocks-analysts.

text.p: The euphoric run-up in technology shares on the Singapore stock exchange in the past month may have further go, analysts said on Tuesday.
In the past month, the Singapore electronics index rocketed about 31 percent to a high of 163 from about 124 on signs of a turnaound in the electronics industry in the second half of the year.
While many have exceeded valuations based on prospects in 1997 and 1998, a few stocks could have more rrom to rise based on earnings expectations and business plans, the analysts said.
David Toh, electronics analyst at ING-Barings, favoured printed circuit-board firms Elec & Eltek and Wong's Circuits.
In particular, Elec & Eltek, currently trading around 15 times its prospective earnings for fiscal year ending June 1998, could have potential to go higher, he said.
It rallied from S$5.50 (US$3.77) in early July to S$7.80 this week. Elec & Eltek was at S$7.35 on Tuesday afternoon.
For the year ended June 1997, Toh expected Elec & Eltek to report a 15 percent net growth to Singapore $56.4 million.
Gregory Tarr, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's Singapore-based technology/electronics analyst said he was bullish on network and systems integrator Datacraft.
"Datacraft is a unique company in network services and is not subject or prone to whatever the PC sales numbers are or Singapore exports numbers are," Tarr said.
"I expect the growth to come in higher than the PE it is currently trading at, so I think Datacraft is still a buy," he said.
He expected Datacraft to report net profit of S$15 million for the full year ended June 1997 compared to S$9.4 million previously. Earnings per share is seen at 7.9 cents.
Datacraft was around S$3.20 Tuesday afternoon. Its shares ran up from about S$2.20 in May to S$3.82 in mid July.
